tldr: For total-treatment-effect estimation under a known directed graph, independent Bernoulli assignment with known \(p=1/2+\varepsilon\), and quadratic schedules satisfying the raw coefficient-mass envelope, the all-estimator minimax risk is uniformly comparable to \(B^2\min\{1,d^2/n+\varepsilon^2\min\{1,d^3/n\}\}\). A computable clipped choice between additive and quadratic SNIPE, with a zero-rule saturation option, attains the upper bound. Separate feasible compact-baseline priors establish the complete-record lower bound for arbitrary Borel estimator kernels. On \((n,d,\varepsilon)=(k^5,k^2,1/(4\sqrt k))\), even clipped full quadratic SNIPE has positive risk uniformly over an explicit family with positive singleton and pair coefficients, while additive and minimax risks vanish. The endpoint comparison gives the precise region of strict asymptotic risk domination. The contribution concerns precision under this fixed design.
